key_insight: CloakFEM shows that valid, solvable FEM programs can exhaust computational resources by dramatically increasing solver work.
engineering_relevance: FEM services may need resource limits and solver-work monitoring because successful input validation alone does not prevent computational denial of service.
method: Use a domain-guided LLM agent to search for adversarial FEM programs.
Represent candidates with an FEM-specific intermediate representation.
Apply a deterministic validity gate to enforce runnable constraints.
evidence_signal: Across 3 FEM stacks, 17 problem classes, and 1,068 seeds, CloakFEM outperformed five generic black-box baselines; the largest iteration increase was from 43 to 247,367 (5,752.72×).
watch_item: The reported maximum measures iteration amplification, not wall-clock slowdown; practical impact depends on the solver and workload.
paper_title: CloakFEM: Agentic FEM Code Generation for Red-Teaming Computational Resource Exhaustion
